Rotation.description: Read-only Core-owned rotation status. Core confirms main-certificate rotation from its own authenticated connection with the new main certificate. Only for a separately issued TAK-only keypair, the trusted observer confirms the first established authenticated TAK connection whose peer-certificate SHA-256 fingerprint matches that active rotation successor. Core then durably and idempotently revokes the mapped predecessor; no manual acknowledgement, CoT transaction or HTTPS probe is required. This is per replacement credential, not proof that all devices sharing the key migrated. A download or client-reported fingerprint is insufficient. An observed main-browser login does not confirm a separate TAK keypair. No silent pre-confirmation retirement timer. Expiry, authorization loss and emergency revocation remain independent. A CA revocation result is separate from OCSP/TAK enforcement. limited explicitly reports a selected asynchronous-session guard or uncovered session behavior, never a zero-traffic guarantee.

confirmationMethod.description: Separate TAK-only keypair rotation uses the first live authenticated TAK connection with the exact approved successor fingerprint. Core-authenticated-use exclusively confirms main-certificate rotation, including when the package reuses that main keypair; operator-verified is an explicit exceptional fallback, never a required additional approval.

info.description: Proposed replacement for legacy TAK RMAPI package delivery. Direct Traefik path routing; no Core product proxy. mTLS plus Core ForwardAuth for protected routes; opaque short-lived token for public downloads. Package creation uses already-issued credentials. Core owns approval, credential purposes, UUID semantics, renewal and revocation. TAK-only issuance resources and private-key Secrets live outside the main user credential namespace. Final Core UI/session contract and TAK 5.8.69 callsign behavior remain separate integration gates. Greenfield implementation target: opendefence/integration-tak, Python package odintegration_tak. The pvarki/python-tak-operator initial_implementation branch is a reference prototype and tooling/CI source, not the repository to extend. TAK accepts the approved main certificate even when its key is client-held, alongside any approved TAK-only certificate for the same UUID. A package contains one exportable keypair. PKCS#12 Java compatibility is preserved. Credential-update variants are gated on exact client/version import validation.
info.title: OpenDefence TAK Integration Package API

get.description: No client certificate required. Treat token as a capability, never log it. Validate its hash and record expiry, then fresh User/credential/purpose/deadline/entitlement state and relevant package revision. Fail closed on authority outage. Reusable until expiry; never consume on GET or HEAD. A supplied invalid TLS certificate may fail the shared-host handshake before HTTP. The credential cannot switch under a grant; current callsign may change. Uniform 404 for malformed, unknown, expired, revoked or no-longer-authorized grants. Do not emit FastAPI-style 422 for invalid public capability inputs. Variant and baseline are taken only from the stored grant. Full packages may render the latest callsign; credential updates omit it. Recheck the authorizing credential as well as the delivered generation and rotation deadlines.

post.description: Requires an approved mTLS principal and ready package. The server binds the grant to one exact credential generation and profile/config/trust revision, while using the latest callsign at redemption. Expiry is capped by 300 seconds, policy deadline and credential validity. Repeated POST may create another grant; active-grant limits bound this. Enforce browser Origin/CSRF policy. Bind full/update variant, base/target revisions and any compatibility ID. No old grant may silently fetch a successor. The high-OPSEC policy requires new-main or independently approved successor-delivery authorization; the old main certificate alone is insufficient.

x-authorization-freshness: Live authorization for grants/content; no reliance solely on a stale informer or UserBinding Synced condition. Document bounded in-flight revocation race; no recall of downloaded keys.
x-callsign-policy: Callsigns are mutable presentation, shared as desired state across credentials. Client editing stays enabled. Document ATAK disablePreferenceItem_locationCallsign as a future, device-tested UI restriction; do not emit it now. Credential-only updates omit callsign.

x-credential-namespaces.apiAccess: No cluster-wide Secret reads; explicit Core export for reused-main material
x-credential-namespaces.takOnly: Dedicated TAK credential namespace or agreed operator namespace, separate from main

x-credential-use-observer: For separately issued TAK-only keypairs only, reuse the guard GroupManager/getUserByConnectionId certificate read in a trusted worker. Core handles all main-certificate confirmation itself; ignore main-certificate TAK connections for rotation confirmation. Persist rotation-generation-bound observations in protected internal status, then let Core trigger idempotent issuer revocation. Do not expose a public confirmation endpoint. Retain this observation capability if upstream TAK removes the need for the optional asynchronous disconnect workaround.
x-design-status: Proposal; not an implemented service. Scope is self-service package delivery. Core enrollment-token auth and delegated downloads require an explicit future Core policy contract, not implicit bearer access.
x-external-identity: Normalize Core UUID ID encoding before comparing to canonical UUID CN. Callsign is presentation only. Track issuer+serial/fingerprint per credential purpose.

x-implementation.processes: Separate JVM-free API, serialized JNI operator and TAK-only credential observer as needed.
x-implementation.repositoryStatus: planned; not created by this audit
x-implementation.tooling: Copy and adapt uv, prek, strict Pyrefly, Ruff, pytest/coverage, Hatchling, versioning and CI from the prototype; rebind publishing and runner configuration.

x-pkcs12-compatibility: Preserve serialize_java_truststore trustedCertEntry behavior, CA filtering, aliases/deduplication and existing public-CA Java-compatible algorithms. Specify private-key export settings separately. Required keytool tests must verify CA trustedCertEntry and client PrivateKeyEntry/chain; skipped Java tests are not release validation.
x-revocation-enforcement: Planned Traefik client-certificate OCSP middleware covers the protected HTTP routes where installed; verify request/handshake placement, verified peer identity on resumption, cache freshness and outage behavior. Raw CoT and existing sessions need separate TAK-side coverage. The inspected subscription-revocation-guard branch reports successful asynchronous disconnects on TAK 5.8-RELEASE-69 but early CoT was delivered. Prefer verified upstream enforcement; an isolated optional companion or no companion remains a deployment decision with explicit residual limits. Never embed this watcher in package API workers or delete the shared UUID account to retire one credential.
x-rotation-policy: Core owns fresh-key issuance and approved purpose cohorts. Proposed high-OPSEC main rotation also rotates TAK-only credentials. Main-certificate rotation is confirmed and revoked by Core when it sees the new main certificate in use, including when that keypair is reused in a TAK ZIP. Separately issued TAK-only keypair rotation revokes its mapped predecessor after the observer reports first established authenticated TAK use of the exact successor fingerprint. Each flow proceeds independently; a main-certificate observation in TAK is not the confirmation path for either flow. Persist evidence with the rotation generation and reject stale observations; no manual confirmation or timer-driven pre-confirmation revocation. Distinct main and TAK-only replacements need their own evidence. Expiry, authorization loss and emergency compromise revocation remain independent. Persist the decision, revoke at the issuer, invalidate grants and verify OCSP/TAK enforcement separately. No successor delivery via stale grants or resurrected revoked keys on rollback.
x-tak-credential-acceptance: Accept approved main plus TAK-only fingerprints under one immutable UUID regardless of main-key exportability. Exact 5.8.69 authentication enforcement must be proved: the inspected public server has scalar fingerprint storage and a username/CN fallback. Do not claim repeated registration creates a fingerprint allowlist.
x-tls-policy: One host/entrypoint must have compatible TLS options. VerifyClientCertIfGiven plus route-level verified-certificate requirements allows both mTLS API operations and certificate-free capability downloads.
